steps.say: For a burst vessel that either treatment could reach, threading coils through the groin gave more patients a good recovery at one year. The price was more late bleeds and repeat procedures than with a metal clip. That trade between early recovery and late durability is what guides every decision today.
steps.tx: **ISAT** (coiling versus clipping trial) took ruptured front-circulation aneurysms that either method could reach. **Coiling** (platinum spirals packed in the sac) gave more patients independence at **1 year** (one year), but late rebleeds and retreatments ran higher than with **clipping** (neck closed with a metal clip), trading early recovery for late durability.

vis.alt: Diagram showing saccular aneurysms on the Circle of Willis, with one ruptured causing subarachnoid hemorrhage.
vis.caption: Saccular aneurysms at Circle of Willis branch points, one ruptured. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: A second trial confirmed the first and mapped out when surgeons still prefer a clip. Clots sitting with the burst vessel, very wide openings and young patients all push toward open surgery. Most other burst aneurysms today are coiled first.
steps.tx: **BRAT** (second clipping-coiling trial) confirmed equipoise with crossover allowed, and practice now coils most ruptured aneurysms. **Clipping** (open neck closure) is still favoured for **middle cerebral bifurcation** (middle-brain fork) haematomas, wide necks and young patients needing **durability** (decades-long fix), where a clip outlasts coils.

steps.say: Clipping opens the skull above the ear and works along the brain surface to the vessel. The surgeon briefly blocks the parent artery, places a permanent clip across the opening, and checks with dye that the branches still fill. Nothing is left inside the bloodstream.
steps.tx: **Clipping** (open neck closure) runs through a **pterional craniotomy** (temple skull opening) with **temporary clipping** (brief parent artery block), then a permanent clip across the neck. **Indocyanine green** (fluorescent dye check) with Doppler confirms parent and branch patency, leaving no metal inside the bloodstream to demand blood thinners.

steps.say: Coiling fills the balloon from the inside with soft platinum spirals delivered through a groin catheter. Wide openings need a stent scaffold or a balloon to hold the spirals in, and any stent means months of two blood thinners. That drug burden is the main cost of stent-assisted coiling.
steps.tx: Simple coiling fills the sac with **detachable coils** (platinum spirals), while **stent-assisted coiling** (mesh scaffold support) and balloon remodelling hold coils in wide-neck aneurysms. Any stent left behind mandates **dual antiplatelets** (a **2** (two) drug blood-thinner pair), since bare metal in the artery invites clot until it heals over.

nodes.label: Wide neck: stent or balloon help

steps.say: Huge and spindle-shaped aneurysms of the carotid are difficult to clip or coil durably. A mesh tube rebuilt the vessel from the inside, and the aneurysm clots off over months. Patients take two blood thinners for half a year while the new lining forms.
steps.tx: **Flow diverters** (vessel-rebuilding mesh tubes) such as the **Pipeline device** (braided carotid stent) reconstruct large or fusiform internal carotid aneurysms from inside. Treatment needs **6 months** (six months) of **dual antiplatelets** (two blood thinners) while occlusion matures over a year, trading immediate closure for gradual vessel healing.

vis.alt: Illustration of thunderclap headache showing ruptured saccular cerebral aneurysm, segmental vasoconstriction, and axial brain CT with star-pattern hemorrhage.
vis.caption: Ruptured saccular aneurysm with subarachnoid blood. Flow diversion is reserved for unruptured large or fusiform carotid aneurysms. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Fork aneurysms with branch vessels at the mouth are the hardest shape of all. A woven wire basket now fills the sac itself without covering the branches, and it needs no long-term blood thinners. That makes it ideal for burst aneurysms at the middle cerebral and anterior communicating forks.
steps.tx: The **WEB device** (woven intrasaccular basket) treats **wide-neck bifurcation** (broad fork opening) aneurysms without dual antiplatelets. It suits ruptured middle cerebral and anterior communicating aneurysms with **branch vessels** (fork arteries) at the neck, filling the sac from within while preserving the daughter branches that stents would jail.

steps.say: Unburst aneurysms found by chance need a different calculus. Big ones, back-circulation ones, pouches with daughter bubbles and young patients are the group that leans toward treatment. Small front-circulation pouches in the elderly are usually watched with repeat scans.
steps.tx: For unruptured aneurysms, size crossing the **7 mm threshold** (seven millimetre mark), a posterior circulation address, **daughter sacs** (secondary pouches) and youth push toward treatment under **ISUIA** (unruptured aneurysm study) rules. Small incidental anterior aneurysms in older patients are usually watched with serial **MRA** (vessel MRI), since 5-year rupture risk there stays below treatment risk.

steps.say: When neither clip nor coil can hold, surgeons fall back on salvage. Wrapping the sac in fabric stops immediate bleeding but the vessel often bursts again. Giant clotted aneurysms may need the whole artery sacrificed with a bypass sewn to feed the brain beyond.
steps.tx: **Wrapping** (fabric coating salvage) or coating is only a last resort when neither clip nor coil can hold, because wrapped aneurysms **rebleed** (burst again). Giant thrombosed aneurysms may instead need **bypass** (replacement blood route) with parent vessel sacrifice, sewing a graft to feed the brain beyond the closed artery.
